kf: **Ingrowing toenail** (onychocryptosis): the nail edge pierces the lateral fold, usually of the **big toe**.
Commonest in teenagers and young men; causes: cutting nails curved or too short, tight shoes, hyperhidrosis, involuted nails.
Stages: inflammation → infection with granulation tissue → chronic fold hypertrophy.
Cut straight across, wide shoes, soaks, lift the edge; antibiotics only for spreading cellulitis.
Recurrent: **partial nail avulsion with phenol** by podiatry (about 95% success). Diabetes or PAD: refer early.

sub: Adolescents and young adults, males more than females; also older people with thickened nails.

aet: Nail cutting, footwear, sweaty feet, trauma, pincer nails.
Drugs: isotretinoin and EGFR inhibitors cause similar periungual granulation.
myths: **"Cut a V in the middle of the nail"**: this does not work; cut straight across.
**"Antibiotics fix it"**: they do not remove the spike of nail.
patho_lead: A **spike of nail** acts as a foreign body in the nail fold.

mech.t: A sharp nail edge pierces the lateral fold, often after cutting the corner short.
The fold becomes red, swollen and painful; bacteria colonise the wound.
Continued irritation produces moist, bleeding 'proud flesh' overhanging the nail.
mech.cap: Ingrowing toenail with granulation tissue on the lateral fold; inset: nail cut straight across.

mech.t: Removing the edge and destroying that strip of matrix (phenol) stops regrowth.

sub: High risk of infection, ulceration and amputation: early podiatry.

prog: Mild cases settle with conservative care; phenol matricectomy rarely recurs.
